objective: Make the task workspace show real work: triage every open task read-only, propose a disposition for each, and prepare a gated script for the bulk changes.
current_state: Read-only triage is authorized by the principal's 2026-09-28 governance ('start now, nothing archived until approved'). The 2026-09-28 sweep through the ClickUp connector returned well over 300 open tasks across three paged queries without exhausting pagination, so the true count is UNKNOWN. Two clusters dominate: daily and weekly cadence instances generated automatically since early September and never closed, and a batch of 200+ undated content-slot tasks created on 2026-09-28 inside a list whose parent folder was retired on 2026-09-10. The connector exposes no bulk operator (clickup_get_operators returned none enabled), so each change is one API call; that is why this is Code work rather than connector work.
verified_facts: Two full pages (200 tasks) of a single workspace-wide query were returned with has_more still true
The content-slot batch carries no due date and no assignee
The recurring cadence instances date back to early September 2026 and are all in 'to do'
sources: Principal's governance session of 2026-09-28 (decision register item 22 and the 'start now without a ruling' list)
assumptions: INFERRED: cadence instances are created by a recurring automation outside ClickUp's own recurrence; which one is UNKNOWN
INFERRED: the content-slot batch was written by an importer into the retired list by mistake rather than by design
decisions: Read-only first. Every write is behind a dry-run manifest and an explicit --apply flag, and the principal approves the manifest list by list
Close, never delete. A status change is reversible; a deletion is not
The API token is read from the CLICKUP_API_TOKEN environment variable and is never written to disk in this repository
The script and its outputs stay out of this public repository; only this non-identifying packet is committed

The workspace spans several capacities. Triage reads across them but moves no task content between capacities; any relocation that would cross a lane or capacity boundary is marked ASK, which is the express authorization the Council protocol requires
open_questions: Where should the content-slot batch live, given the pending ruling on how The Excellence District, H.O.P.E. Dealers and Primerica relate (HDPR-002)?
Should stale cadence instances be closed, or should the generating automation be stopped first?
Should the list that serves as the content approval gate be excluded from triage writes entirely? Recommended: yes
risks: Closing instances that the Watchdog or a review reads as evidence of activity would change what those reviews report
A bulk move into the wrong capacity's list is a lane-firewall breach even if it is reversible
Rate limits: ClickUp throttles bulk calls; the script must back off rather than retry in a tight loop
dependencies: A ClickUp personal API token supplied by the principal at run time
HDPR-002 ruling before the content-slot batch is relocated
required_output: Disposition table (local, uncommitted) with a per-cluster summary returned to the principal
A return handoff on this bus stating counts only
human_gate: Principal approves the dry-run manifest, list by list, before any write. HDPR-002 must be ruled before the content-slot batch moves.
last_action: Swept the workspace read-only through the connector, confirmed no bulk operator exists, and scoped the work.
next_action: Export every open task via the API to a local file, reconcile the count against 305, then draft the disposition table.
rollback: Nothing has been written to ClickUp. When writes are later approved, the manifest records each task's prior status and list so every change can be reversed from it.
